exchanges: I need to vent about a client meeting and then probably get your help drafting an email.
Happy to do both. What happened in the meeting?
So the client is a regional bank, and their marketing contact, Hannah, wanted to completely change the campaign direction three days before launch. Three days!
That's a painful amount of change that close to launch. Did she explain what prompted it?
Apparently their CEO, Mr. Lindqvist, saw the draft and hated the colours. Which, fine, but we sent it two weeks ago.
So the delay was on their side. That's worth noting politely in whatever you send back.
Exactly. And Hannah was on the call from home because she's on crutches, she rolled her ankle playing squash last weekend and it's apparently a bad sprain.
Ouch, that'll slow anyone down. Maybe that's part of why the review got delayed.
Maybe. Anyway I came back to the office and told Adaeze, she's my boss, and she just laughed and said welcome to banking clients.
Sounds like she's seen this before. Did she have any advice?
She said push back on the timeline, not the changes. She's very strategic, she did her MBA at INSEAD and she treats everything like a case study.
That's good advice, though. Accepting the feedback but resetting the date keeps the relationship intact.

True. Okay, the funny part is that our junior designer is also named Hannah, and she's also injured right now. She fell off her bike and fractured her wrist, so she's doing all the redesigns one-handed.
That's quite the coincidence. Redesigning a campaign with one hand sounds really hard, though.
She's a trooper. She uses a drawing tablet with her left hand now and honestly it's not bad.
That's impressive adaptability. Still, it might be worth giving her extra time on the new version.
Agreed. So for the email, I want to say we'll make the colour changes but we need to move launch by a week.
Here's a start: 'Thanks for the feedback. We're happy to update the palette and will need to move the launch date by one week to do it properly.' Want it warmer or more formal?
Warmer, but firm. Lindqvist is old school, he likes formal, but Hannah is the one reading it.
Then a friendly opening and a clear, firm line on the date. You can keep a formal sign-off for Lindqvist's sake.
Perfect. I'll write it up and you can check it.
Sounds good, send it over when it's ready.
Before I do, Dmitri just stopped by my desk. He's our copywriter. He's been learning Portuguese for a trip next year and wanted to practice on me, and I don't speak a word of it.
That's a brave approach to practicing. Did you at least nod along convincingly?
I said 'obrigado' about ten times. That's all I've got.
That's a perfectly respectable vocabulary for a coworker practice session.

Okay, here's the draft: Hi Hannah, thanks for passing along the feedback. We can absolutely update the palette. To do this properly, we'll need to move launch by one week. Hope your recovery is going well.
That's clear and kind. You might add one line with the new date so there's no ambiguity.
Good point. I'll add 'new launch date: the 21st.' Sent!
Nice, done and dusted. Now you wait.
She already replied. She said yes to the new date. I'm shocked.
That's a great outcome. It sounds like the firm-but-warm approach worked.
Adaeze is going to be smug about it.
She did call it. A little smugness is earned.
Lunch time. I'm getting the soup from the place downstairs.
Enjoy, you've had a productive morning.
Back. Ugh, I said something wrong earlier. Dmitri isn't learning Portuguese, it's Japanese. The trip is to Osaka. I think I mixed it up with his wife, she's the one from Brazil.
That makes more sense with Osaka. Sounds like a language-heavy household.
Very. Their kids are going to be trilingual.
Lucky kids. That's a real head start.
Okay, now I need to plan the redesign schedule with designer Hannah.
Since she's working one-handed, maybe split the work into smaller pieces with check-ins.
Good idea. Three check-ins over the week.
That gives you room to catch problems early without micromanaging.
Adaeze wants to sit in on the final one.
Having her there should help get it approved quickly.
Probably. She's leaving early today though. Her mom is visiting.
That's nice. Is her mom coming from far away?
Very far. She's flying in from Enugu, it's her first visit to Canada in like six years, so Adaeze is a bit nervous about everything being perfect.
Six years is a long gap, no wonder she wants it to go well. I hope they have a wonderful visit.
Me too. She's taking the rest of the week off.
Well deserved, and good timing now that the client crisis is handled.
Right. Okay, I'm going to start on the schedule.
Good luck. Let me know if you want help laying it out.

questions.message: What did Hannah at the bank hurt again? I want to ask how she's healing.
Which business school did Adaeze go to?
Dmitri's practicing Japanese for his vacation, right?
Where is Adaeze's mom travelling from?
Where did Lindqvist go to school, do you know?
I think I'll block out tomorrow morning for deep work.
